_about: Schema-valid planner drafts (Proposal, see packages/core/src/reality/proposal.ts) for questions that are not built-in examples, used to prove that AI-drafted maps reach the adaptive scenery (Phase 2). Written by hand in the planner's format and checked by validateProposal in packages/web/src/atlas/environment/universes.test.ts; served by intercepting POST /api/plan, never sent to a provider. Numbers are left unknown, as the planner leaves them.

What if I started my own independent gam.interpretation: You are thinking about leaving salaried work to make games independently. I compared building a first game on your own savings, building it with a publisher's support, and keeping your job while making games in your spare time.

branches.name: Self-funded indie studio
branches.description: Leave your job and build a first game on your savings, working from a rented studio.

branches.name: Publisher-backed team
branches.description: Pitch a prototype and build the game with a publisher's advance, sharing a co-working office.

branches.name: Keep my job, make games at night
branches.description: Stay employed and build the game in your spare time at home.

variables.label: How the work is paid for
variables.why: Decides how long you can work before the game earns anything.

variables.label: Where the work happens
variables.why: Changes monthly costs and how you work with other people.

variables.label: Monthly costs
variables.why: Rent, tools, licences and living costs while you build.

variables.label: Savings available
variables.why: How long you can keep going without an income.

variables.label: Months until the first release
variables.why: Most of the risk comes before the first game is out.

variables.label: Team size
variables.why: More people can shorten the work but raise the costs.

questions: How many months of living costs do your savings cover?
Would a publisher want to see a prototype first?

formulas.label: Months the savings last
formulas.explanation: Only counts savings against costs; any income from the game is left out.

possibilities.text: Full creative control over the game
Savings run out before the game is finished
Deadlines and milestones set by the publisher

possibilities.branch: Keep my job, make games at night
possibilities.text: Slower progress with less financial pressure
The first game earns less than hoped

missingEvidence: A publisher's terms for a first game
limitations: Sales, platform fees and taxes are not modelled.

What if I opened a small café in my neig.interpretation: You are considering opening a café near where you live. I compared running a small café yourself, hiring a barista from the start, and testing the idea with a coffee cart first.

branches.name: Small café, run by me
branches.description: A café with a few tables, open mornings and lunchtimes, with you behind the counter.

branches.name: Café with a hired barista
branches.description: The same café, with a barista hired from the first day.

branches.name: Coffee cart at the market first
branches.description: Sell coffee from a cart on market days before taking on a lease.

variables.label: Format
variables.why: Sets the rent, the fit-out and how many people you can serve.

variables.label: Hire a barista
variables.why: Adds wages but frees your time.

variables.label: Staff on shift
variables.why: How many people serve at once.

variables.label: Rent
variables.why: Usually the largest fixed cost.

variables.label: Cups sold per day
variables.why: Depends on footfall and opening hours.

variables.label: Price per cup
variables.why: Set by you, compared with nearby cafés.

variables.label: Cost per cup
variables.why: Coffee, milk, cups and card fees.

questions: How many people pass the shopfront in the morning?
What would the lease and fit-out cost?

formulas.label: Takings per day
formulas.explanation: Drinks only; food is left out.

possibilities.text: More time to run the business

possibilities.branch: Coffee cart at the market first
possibilities.text: Regular customers before any lease is signed

limitations: Food sales, equipment and taxes are not modelled.

What if our town council chose to restor.interpretation: Your town council is deciding how to reduce flooding from the river. I compared restoring the wetlands upstream, building higher flood walls along the town, and doing both in stages.

branches.name: Restore the wetlands
branches.description: Let the river spread into restored wetlands upstream when it rises.

branches.name: Build higher flood walls
branches.description: Raise the walls along the river where it passes the town.

branches.name: Wetlands first, walls later
branches.description: Restore the wetlands now and raise the walls where they are still needed.

variables.label: Flood approach
variables.why: The decision itself.

variables.label: Homes at risk of flooding
variables.why: From the flood maps for the town.

variables.label: Cost to the council
variables.why: Needs estimates from engineers and ecologists.

variables.label: Years to complete
variables.why: Wetlands take time to establish.

variables.label: Wetland area restored
variables.why: How much land can hold water when the river rises.

questions: Which land upstream could hold water?
How high would the walls need to be?
Who owns the land along the river?

formulas.label: Cost per home protected
formulas.explanation: Treats every home at risk as protected, which neither approach guarantees.

possibilities.text: More birds and wildlife along the river
Views of the river are blocked in the town
Protection builds up over a longer time
Heavier storms than the plans allow for

limitations: Insurance, property values and downstream effects are not modelled.

What if I could talk to my future self o.interpretation: An imagined situation: one conversation a year with yourself from the future. I compared asking about the big decisions, asking only about everyday things, and choosing never to ask.

branches.name: Ask about the big decisions
branches.description: Use each conversation to ask about the choices that matter most.

branches.name: Ask about everyday things
branches.description: Keep the conversations light: small choices and how things feel.

branches.name: Never ask
branches.description: Know the conversation is possible, and choose not to have it.

variables.label: What you would ask about
variables.why: The choice this map is about.

variables.label: How far you would trust the answers
variables.why: Changes how much each answer would shape what you do.

variables.label: Days spent preparing each year
variables.why: Time spent thinking about what to ask.

questions: What would you most want to know?
Would you change anything after hearing it?

possibilities.text: Choices start to feel decided in advance
Curiosity about the answers that were never heard

limitations: An imagined situation: there is nothing to measure.
